title: FIFA Squad Deadline Day — All 48 Nations Submit Final 26-Man Rosters; Official Lists to Publish June 2
detail: June 1, 2026 marked the official FIFA final squad submission deadline for all 48 nations competing in the FIFA World Cup 2026. Teams had until end of day to register their 26-man squads (minimum 3 goalkeepers) with FIFA, with all confirmed lists scheduled for simultaneous publication on June 2. Among the nations submitting on deadline day were Australia (coached by Tony Popovic) and Ecuador. Major squads already confirmed in the lead-up: USA (May 26), Brazil (May 18), Netherlands (May 27), Argentina (May 30), England (May 22), Germany (May 21), France (May 14), Portugal (May 19), Japan (May 15), South Korea (May 16). Iran's submission was the most closely watched on deadline day — their football federation submitted their 26-man roster led by captain Mehdi Taremi (Inter Milan) despite not a single US entry visa having been issued to any Iranian delegation member by the US State Department. The squad freeze also locks in tournament-changing selection calls: Lionel Messi (six World Cups, equalling Ronaldo's record), Manuel Neuer's comeback for Germany, and the late inclusion of England's Ivan Toney and France's Rayan Cherki. FIFA's June 2 publication of all 48 confirmed rosters marks the final pre-tournament roster picture ahead of the June 11 opening match at Estadio Azteca. 10 days to kickoff.

title: Mexico 1-0 Australia — Final Pre-World Cup Friendly; El Tri Arrive in Tournament Form Ahead of June 11 Opener vs South Africa
detail: Mexico defeated Australia 1-0 in an international friendly on June 1, 2026 — El Tri's final pre-tournament warm-up before the FIFA World Cup 2026 opens at Estadio Azteca 10 days later. Javier Aguirre's side enter the tournament in confident form, having now won consecutive pre-tournament friendly matches. Mexico open the World Cup on June 11 at Estadio Azteca against South Africa — one of the most anticipated fixtures of the opening weekend given the historic symbolism of Mexico hosting at the Azteca for a third time (having previously hosted in 1970 and 1986). Australia, coached by Tony Popovic, were among the nations submitting their squad to FIFA on the official June 1 deadline day. The Socceroos face the USMNT in Group D (June 21, NRG Stadium Houston) — making this match a useful pre-tournament scouting exercise for Mauricio Pochettino's coaching staff. With all pre-tournament matches now concluded, both nations depart for their designated tournament bases ahead of the June 11 kickoff.

title: Iran Squad Deadline Passes With Zero US Visas — 10 Days to Group G Opener; Tijuana Base Camp Fully Operational; Forfeiture Risk Escalates
detail: The FIFA squad submission deadline of June 1 passed without a single US entry visa being issued to any member of Iran's World Cup delegation — the sharpest escalation yet in the visa crisis with exactly 10 days remaining to Iran's June 15 Group G opener vs New Zealand at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. Iran's football federation submitted their 26-man squad on deadline day, headed by captain Mehdi Taremi (Inter Milan), goalkeeper Alireza Beiranvand, Alireza Jahanbakhsh (Feyenoord), and Saman Ghoddos (Brentford). Iran's base camp at Centro Xoloitzcuintle in Tijuana is now fully operational, with the squad training daily in Mexico and planning to commute across the US-Mexico border for Group G matches at SoFi Stadium (June 15 vs New Zealand; June 21 vs Belgium) and Lumen Field, Seattle (June 26 vs Egypt). Iran's federation president Mehdi Taj formally demanded clarification from FIFA that players would receive multiple-entry visas given the cross-border logistics. FIFA provided written guarantees of visa issuance but the US State Department has given no confirmed timeline. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has stated the concern is not athletes but IRGC-linked support staff seeking to enter with the delegation. The American Immigration Council confirmed fans from Iran remain under an absolute B-2 tourist visa ban. If no visas are issued before June 15, Iran would face potential forfeiture — an unprecedented situation in World Cup history. FIFA has not publicly addressed what consequence mechanism would apply. 50 additional countries face a $15,000 USD visa bond requirement for tournament travel.

media.caption: Iran's World Cup squad at Tijuana base camp — squad deadline passes with zero US visas issued, 10 days to Group G opener vs New Zealand
